facts.statement: A Chinese-Canadian expedition discovered the remains of Sinornithoides near Huamuxiao in the Ordos Basin of Inner Mongolia in 1988.
facts.quote: In 1988, a Chinese-Canadian expedition discovered the remains of a small theropod near Huamuxiao, in the Ordos Basin of Inner Mongolia.

facts.statement: The species Sinornithoides youngi was named and described in 1993 or 1994 by Dale Russell and Dong Zhiming.
facts.quote: Sinornithoides youngi, the type species, was named and described in 1993/1994 by Dale Russell and Dong Zhiming based on this fossil specimen from the Lower Cretaceous Ejinhoro Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V9612 is an almost complete, articulated skeleton missing only the roof of the skull and some vertebrae.
facts.quote: It is represented by a holotype, IVPP V9612, an almost complete skeleton with skull, which is articulated and nearly complete except for the roof of the skull, some cervical and many dorsal vertebrae, along with some other referred skeletal elements.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen represents a subadult individual.
Sinornithoides measured approximately 1 meter in length and likely ate invertebrates and other small prey.
facts.quote: Sinornithoides measured approximately 1 m long, and probably ate invertebrates and other small prey.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the body length of Sinornithoides at 1.1 meters and its weight at 2.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its body length at 1.1 metres, its weight at 2.5 kilogrammes.

facts.statement: As a troodontid, Sinornithoides possessed sickle-claws, raptorial hands, and a high encephalization quotient indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
facts.quote: Troodontids have sickle-claws and raptorial hands, and some of the highest non-avian encephalization quotients, meaning they were behaviourally advanced and had keen senses.

facts.statement: The skull of Sinornithoides contained four premaxillary teeth and about twenty-three maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: There are four premaxillary and about twenty-three maxillary teeth.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen preserves a furcula and a basket consisting of fifteen pairs of gastralia.
facts.quote: The holotype preserves a furcula and a basket of fifteen pairs of gastralia.

facts.statement: The sickle claw on the second toe of Sinornithoides is relatively large and long compared to other troodontids.
facts.quote: The sickle claw of the second toe is relatively large and long for a troodontid.

facts.statement: Sinornithoides lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian or Albian stages around 113 million years ago, in Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Sinornithoides (meaning "Chinese bird form") is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaurs that lived during the Early Cretaceous (Aptian or Albian stage, around 113 million years ago) of Inner Mongolia, China.

facts.statement: Sinornithoides youngi lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, 113 million years ago, during the Albian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Sinornithoides youngi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Sinornithoides ("con forma de ave china") de dinosaurio terópodo trodóntido, que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace 113 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Sinornithoides spans the Albian stage from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 1994, Sinornithoides was assigned to the family Troodontidae.
facts.quote: Sinornithoides was in 1994 assigned to the Troodontidae.

facts.statement: Despite the lack of sufficient comparative fossil material to identify diagnostic traits, Sinornithoides was assigned to the Troodontidae family.
A 2012 analysis by Turner, Makovicky, and Norell shows a possible position for Sinornithoides in the evolutionary tree of Paraves.
facts.quote: Una posible posición de Sinornithoides en el árbol evolutivo de los Paraves se muestra por el cladograma a continuación, siguiendo un análisis de 2012 por Turner, Makovicky y Norell.

facts.statement: The generic name Sinornithoides means "Chinese bird form," derived from Latin and Greek roots referencing its bird-like build.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin Sinae, "Chinese", and Greek ὄρνις, ornis, "bird", en ~ειδής, ~eides, a suffix meaning "~like", in reference to the bird-like build.

facts.statement: The specific name youngi honors the paleontologist Yang Zhongjian.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Yang Zhongjian.

rejected.statement: The holotype skeleton is preserved in a roosting position with its snout tucked under its left hand.
rejected.quote: The holotype is preserved in much the same roosting position as another troodontid fossil, that of Mei long, with its snout tucked under its left hand.
